A proof picks its app through `tools/proof/proof_app.py`: `RC_PROOF_APP` is
`debug` (the default), `release` or a `.app` path. `mcp.launch`, `mcp.MCP` and
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` refuse a tree's built app when any
input is newer than its last complete build (its
`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`), or an instance started before an input
changed, naming the file, its time and the `make` target.

Release-only proofs pass `release_only=` (`git grep release_only= tools/proof`);
recording_proof's socket instance is started with
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release`.

**Before trusting any MCP proof, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`
must print nothing** — that prefix is the startup parity check complaining.
On a Debug build the same complaint is an `assertionFailure` that traps first
(`AgentServer.prepareCatalog`), so `make app-debug` fails at Write Agent
Catalog with `Fatal error: …` instead of logging the line.

A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults domain (the owner's
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for a Release build, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for a Debug build, spec §11 V-5): no
environment moves `UserDefaults` (#238). Never perform a persisting menu item
(View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview
Quality) on either build: `mcp.py` ends the script with status 3 and
`DEFAULTS MOVED` last on stderr when its session moved a key and no other
Frame Job shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does;
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. The guard reads the domain with
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` taken out of `defaults`' environment
(`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a proof run under a scratch home that does
not exist yet, or is removed before the script ends, is compared with
itself: `defaults export` answers no key under a variable naming an absent
folder.

**`tools/proof/` holds the scripts that do this** — an MCP script per phase
over a dependency-free client (`mcp.py`), and beside most of them an
offscreen-chrome script or a probe. Every claim in them is a placement read
back through `get_project`, a BYTE comparison of two PNGs, or a
sample-for-sample comparison of two exports decoded to PCM (which needs
`ffmpeg` at proof time). Its README says how to make the test media, run
one, and which scores are known host-state skips (a locked console, a
Bluetooth output). Add the next phase's proof there rather than writing a
throwaway. Every open document costs an instance threads and memory
(`tools/proof/README.md`, "Relaunch the instance between proof sessions", has
the measured cost and what closing one gives back): a proof that closes what
it opens (`close_project`) can share an instance, and one that does not
relaunches between proof sessions.

Spec §10's per-step verifications are the acceptance tests. What no script
can answer — step 4's "the clip plays with audio", step 5's 60 fps, and the
rest — is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, which the owner runs.

## Verification

- **In the loop:** a targeted test (`cd core && cargo test --release --test
  <file> <filter>`), `make lint` after Rust edits, `make typecheck` after Swift
  edits, `make app-debug` before driving the app, and the phase's own rows
  (`--only` where the proof has it) against Debug.
- **Once, when the code is complete:** `make gate`, in the foreground, under
  the 600 s tool cap (`make gate GATE_ARGS=--force` only when a stamp itself is
  in doubt). It stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and
  tools are byte-identical to its last pass, so after a fix it re-runs only
  what the fix can change. Never run one of its steps by hand to stand in for
  it, never re-run an unchanged step, and never run anything twice with no
  edit between.
- **The proof a phase records** runs whole once, on the final instrument,
  against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release` after the gate's `make app`), with
  any `release_only` proof the change touches. This is a rule: nothing checks
  which build a recorded run drove.
- **A proof that fails only on Debug** is pinned `release_only="<reason>"` in
  the change that finds it (spec §11 V-4); an assert trap on Debug is a defect
  to fix, never a pin.
- **Mutants** target the decisions the phase adds: about one per new branch,
  threshold, refusal or ordering, usually 3–8; more than 10 only with a reason
  written in the spec. The full set runs once, at the end, on the final
  instrument. A mutant's anchor is counted by `tools/proof/mutant_anchors.py` in
  `make test`: a proof taking `--mutant` holds its mutants in a top-level
  table (tree text as file, anchor, replacement; switches as names), and a new
  table shape or a mutant with no tree text gets its row there in the same
  change, and a table's expression stays pure, because the check evaluates it.
- **A fix pass** re-runs only the rows whose instrument code it changed and
  the mutants whose anchor lines it touched, then `make gate`.
- **Background** only for a command that cannot fit 600 s, waited on once with
  a bound; never a poll loop.

## Seeing the chrome

`screencapture` needs a Screen Recording grant the agent's terminal may or
may not have (it varies by host and session), and without it `screencapture`
silently writes a black PNG. Assume neither: a proof that needs the grant
probes for it and skips its granted tier by name, and a capture is never
trusted until it is checked non-black. The way to LOOK at the chrome is
**`tools/proof/harness/`**: it compiles every file in `app/Sources` except
`main.swift` with a `main.swift` of its own, links the staticlib, opens a
`.framejob` package, puts an `EditorViewController` in an `NSWindow` and
`cacheDisplay`s it into a PNG at the display's backing scale — the same paint
path the window uses, no TCC grant, either appearance, captured on SETTLE.
The preview well comes out as the canvas background (an `AVPlayerLayer` or
Metal layer does not draw into `cacheDisplay`), so nothing about the PICTURE
is ever claimed offscreen; pixel claims go over MCP. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"offscreen harness" section has the build line, the argument list and the
pinned `UserDefaults`.

To look at the LIVE app, a Debug or Release build (`make app-debug`,
`make app`; never Distribution) has dev tools over MCP (road map 11, spec §11 V-1).
`snapshot_ui` captures the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel, with a
layout dump. `perform_menu_item` runs a menu item by path to put a sheet or
Settings up, `cancel_sheet` closes the sheet, and `select_inspector_tab`
picks an inspector tab and sub-tab. All four work with the
app inactive and its window covered. A capture's look is set at launch with
the dev-only `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, never switched live. Its scale is
`-RCDevCaptureScale 1|2|3` (spec §11 #539), which `screens.py` pins to 2, so a
capture is 2× on a 1× display without moving a window. To see every
catalogued screen at once, `python3 tools/proof/screens.py` walks
`designs/screens/`, once per look, each time on its own pinned instance. It
writes each screen's PNGs and layout dumps and one `screens.md` with the
prose and each capture's layout problems. The last screen is the recorder
panel: shown from the background it no longer takes key (#137), but an
instance that is active when it runs still gets a key panel with Record on
Return, so the script stops each instance straight after capturing it.

Two rules from it worth carrying into any proof: **identical, stable,
DIFFERENT output across processes is an Auto Layout ambiguity to find, not a
race to out-wait** — reach for constraint priorities, not for more run-loop
turns (on an `NSStackView` that is `setHuggingPriority(_:for:)`;
`setContentHuggingPriority` is inert on a stack); and **when the thing to
check is app ARITHMETIC or app STRUCTURE with
no caller a script can reach** (a menu, a validator, a cue builder, a queue),
the answer is a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through
`tools/proof/swift_build.py`, not a photograph. A probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit, so a rotted instrument cannot take a score down with
it. **That rule applies to historical instruments too.** The meter and welcome
comparisons build old `app/Sources` with the matching old core and header in
isolated output directories, using the current guarded `harness/main.swift`
for both paints; `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s W and SP baselines build the
same way through `reference_build.py`, each in its own folder. A proof that
compares with the base's built APP (`co2a_proof.py` D15, `ramp_proof.py` U1)
finds its base with `tree_copy.default_base()` and builds it whole with

   on the same lane; check). It starts the 30 days when it is the first.
2. When the ask is due, the Tips window opens after such an export completes,
   as it does after a queued export a person added. It must not block or
   delay any further MCP call (it is already a non-modal window ordered front
   without taking key; verify that holds from the agent door, including with
   the app inactive, with no editor window, and for a document opened with no
   window).
3. This amends the TIP entries; the owner decided it, so amend them in place
   and say what changed, before the code.

## The hard part: proofs

The original reason for excluding agent exports stands for PROOF instances,
and must still be solved:

- Proof instances export over MCP constantly and share the bundle's defaults
  domain (the owner's real `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for Release proofs).
  They must not count exports, move the owner's Tips state, trip
  `mcp.py`'s `DEFAULTS MOVED` guard, or put a Tips window into a
  `snapshot_ui` capture, a screens.py run, or any proof's window list.
- So the app needs a way to tell a proof-launched instance from a person's
  instance driven by their own agent, and the proofs' launcher
  (`tools/proof/proof_app.py`, `mcp.launch`, the harness, probes) must use it
  on every path. Find how proofs launch (arguments, environment, the socket
  path) and choose the mechanism: it must be one place, impossible for a new
  proof to forget (this codebase is agents-only: a trap must self-adjust or
  fail loudly in `make test`), and must not be something an ordinary user's
  MCP client sets by accident. If it is a launch switch, decide whether it is
  a product switch or `-RCDev…` (dev switches are compiled out of
  Distribution, and `dist_check.py` checks that); note Distribution builds are
  never launched by proofs.
- Also consider the owner's own agent sessions on the installed app: those
  are real use and SHOULD count under the new rule.
- The tips proof itself needs a way to see an agent export count and the
  window open (in an isolated state: it must not move the real domain), and
  mutants for the new decisions (agent export counted; proof instance not
  counted; window does not block the next call).

## Constraints

Same as the first Tips change: pure schedule untouched unless needed; no new
menu item; file caps; frozen files take wiring only; docs site page
(`docs/site/src/content/docs/reference/tips.mdx`) and `features.json` row
corrected (they say only exports you made count); `docs/manual-checks.md` if a
person-only check changes; agents never edit any `CLAUDE.md` (list edits
owed). Verification: `make typecheck` in the loop, the tips proof on Debug and
on Release with its mutants, then `make gate` once in the foreground or, if it
cannot fit 600 s, in the background waited on once. Do not commit, stage, push
or merge.

below are relative to it. Nothing was changed.

## Goal

1. **Agent exports count.** A completed export started by the `export` tool (an MCP client over
   the socket or `framejob-mcp`, or the in-app Assistant) counts toward Tips exactly as a
   person's Add to Queue job does, and stamps the first-export date when it is the first.
2. **The window opens after them.** When the ask is due, the Tips window is shown when such a
   job completes, front and never key, and no later tool call waits on it.
3. **The spec says so first.** TIP-3, TIP-4, TIP-5 and TIP-7 are amended in place, each saying
   what changed, and one new entry (TIP-8) records who counts.
4. **Proof instances still count nothing.** An instance a proof launches writes no Tips key,
   shows no Tips window, and needs nothing a new proof could forget.

## What is true now

- **The agent's door is deliberately unfollowed.** `AgentServer.exportProject` enqueues and
  tracks, and never tells Tips (`app/Sources/AgentServer+Export.swift:86-99`). The only callers
  of `TipsDoors` are the export card's two commits
  (`app/Sources/EditorViewController+Export.swift:67`, `:104`). TIP-4 states the exclusion
  (`designs/spec/11-decisions/tips.md:47-63`), and the proof holds it three ways: T1's text
  count, L2, and the mutant `agent-follows` (`tools/proof/tips_proof.py:291-301`, `:403-417`,
  `:179-183`).
- **The Assistant's export is the same handler.** `AssistantSession` submits to
  `AgentLane.submit` (`AssistantSession.swift:306`), which routes to `AgentServer.execute` and
  the one handler table (`AgentLane.swift:193-199`, `AgentServer.swift:331`). The request's
  "check" holds: one line in `exportProject` covers both callers.
- **The window cannot make a call wait.** `showAutomatic()` is `orderFront(nil)` on a window
  modal to nothing (`TipsWindowController.swift:117-121`). A followed job's ask runs from the
  queue's own notification on main (`:193-199`), outside every tool call and outside the lane's
  lock. Nothing in `AgentLane.onMainWhenIdle` (`AgentLane.swift:240-251`) looks at windows. So
  item 2 needs no change to the window, only the follow.
- **`follow(queueJob:)` already handles the agent's early refusal.** It settles at once
  (`Tips.swift:155-158`), and a job that failed inside `enqueue` is dropped (`:169-170`).
- **Every instance a proof drives has `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` set.** `mcp.launch` sets it
  unconditionally (`tools/proof/mcp.py:609-610`); `proof_app.py launch` goes through it
  (`proof_app.py:408-409`); every own-`Popen` proof I found sets it too
  (`agent_socket_proof.py:310`, `mcp_proxy_proof.py:215`, `defaults_proof.py:203`, `:403`,
  `mc1_spike.py:676`), because it is the only way to reach an instance that is not on the
  owner's socket (spec §11 MC-6, restated at `AgentServer+Socket.swift:16-18`). The proxy
  already calls this "a scratch instance" (`mcp-proxy/src/socket.rs`, `is_scratch`) and the
  site calls it a test copy (`docs/site/src/content/docs/mcp/connect-a-client.mdx:90-100`).
- **A probe can reach the handler in process.** `assistant_lane_probe.swift:378`, `:386`,
  `:624` submit `export` through the lane in a bare executable with neither variable set
  (`assistant_lane_proof.py:126-134`). Today every one is declined before the handler, so
  nothing completes, but the door is reachable.
- **`snapshot_ui {}` lists every visible window with `title` and `key`**
  (`UISnapshot.swift:130-137`, `:168-181`), so a live row can see the Tips window without a
  new tool. `perform_menu_item` refuses while an app-modal window is up
  (`AgentServer+MenuItem.swift:194-198`), so it is a direct read of "modal to nothing".
- **The request's premise about launch paths is slightly off.** The offscreen harness and the
  probes are bare executables that bind no socket and are not "launched" through
  `proof_app.py`; the mechanism below covers them by what they are, not by a launcher change.
  `mcp.py` and `proof_app.py` need no edit.

## Change

### 0. Spec, before any code (`designs/spec/11-decisions/tips.md`, its `README.md`, `designs/spec/README.md`)

- **TIP-4, rewritten in place**, opening "(amended 2026-11-14, the owner: 'Exports over the
  MCP count…')" and saying what it replaced. Every export that completes in a person's
  instance (TIP-8) counts, whoever started it: the card's two commits, an MCP client's
  `export`, the Assistant's `export`. The agent's job is followed by id through the same
  `TipsDoors.follow(queueJob:)` as Add to Queue. The ask is shown when the job completes,
  front and never key. Risks accepted: Frame Job is usually in the background when an agent's
  export ends, so the window waits there, and when the person returns it may become the key
  window, where Return is Leave a Tip; a client that exports in a loop is asked once.
- **TIP-3**: the sentence that a launch-stamped date "would count use by agents alone" is
  corrected (agents' exports are use now; a launch is still not, since a proof also launches).
- **TIP-5**: "written only at a person's doors" becomes "written only in a person's instance
  (TIP-8): when an export succeeds, whoever started it, and at Leave a Tip".
- **TIP-7**: amended. The feature has ONE dev switch, `-RCDevTipsSuite <name>` (below), and
  why; the live rows; the mutant count (eighteen) and the reason each stands.
- **TIP-8, new: a scratch instance counts nothing and asks nothing.** An instance is a
  person's only when all three hold: it runs from an app bundle (`Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier`
  is not nil), `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` is unset or empty, and `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` is unset or empty.
  Risk accepted: a person who runs their everyday copy with `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` set is never
  counted or asked (the site already says that variable is for testing).
- Index: the TIP-4, TIP-5, TIP-7 rows and the file's blurb rewritten, a TIP-8 row, the Lines
  cells (`spec_index_proof.py` checks them). `designs/spec/07.4-swift-file-map.md`'s Tips row
  corrected ("the two export doors `EditorViewController+Export.swift` calls").

### 1. The instance rule (`app/Sources/Tips.swift`, Foundation only, 176 lines now)

```swift
enum TipsInstance {
    static func counts(environment: [String: String], bundleIdentifier: String?) -> Bool
    static let isPersons: Bool   // the process's own, read once
}
```

- `counts` is pure: three guards, one per condition of TIP-8. The socket key is
  `AgentServer.socketEnvironmentKey`, and "empty is unset" matches `socketPlan`
  (`AgentServer+Socket.swift:58`).
- **Why these three, and not a launcher flag.** A flag (`-RCDevProof`, or an environment
  variable set in `bounded.child_env`) is something an own-`Popen` proof forgets, and there
  are dozens of those. The socket variable cannot be forgotten: without it a proof has no
  instance to talk to. `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` closes the one other route to a non-owner socket
  (the default path under a scratch home). The bundle condition covers probes and the
  harness, which call app code in a bare executable. None is something an MCP client sets by
  accident: a client's configuration reaches the helper, and the helper passes the variable to
  the app only for a scratch socket (`mcp-proxy/src/launch.rs`, `open_arguments`).
- **It is a product rule, not `-RCDev`.** It holds in Distribution too, where it means "a test
  copy on its own socket is not counted".
- The loud backstop already exists: a proof instance that counted would write
  `FrameJobTipsExports`, and `mcp.py`'s guard ends the script with status 3.

### 2. The doors (`app/Sources/TipsWindowController.swift`, 239 lines now)

- `TipsDoors.init` gains `counts: @escaping () -> Bool = { TipsInstance.isPersons }`.
- `exportSucceeded(sheetOn:)` and `follow(queueJob:)` each begin `guard counts() else
  { return }`. Both doors, so the rule is "this instance", not "this door"; a scratch instance
  makes no follower and no observer.
- Comments at `:138-142` and `Tips.swift:19`, `:83-85` corrected (no longer "a person's
  door" only).

### 3. The agent's door (`app/Sources/AgentServer+Export.swift`, 310 lines, not frozen)

- `exportProject(_ a:)` keeps its signature (the frozen `AgentServer.swift:331` table is
  untouched) and forwards to `exportProject(_ a: [String: Any], tips: TipsDoors) throws ->
  String` with `.shared`. The probe calls the two-argument form. If the table's
  `{ $0.exportProject }` turns ambiguous, the builder renames the inner one; the probe is its
  only other caller.
- Inside the existing main block, after `AgentExports.shared.track(…)`:
  `tips.follow(queueJob: id)`. The doc comment says the job counts toward Tips (TIP-4).
- `EditorViewController+Export.swift:91-94`'s comment "The agent's `export` enqueues without
  this" is corrected. No code change there.

### 4. The proof's one dev switch (`app/Sources/Tips.swift`, under `#if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`)

`-RCDevTipsSuite <name>`: `TipsAsk.shared` reads and writes `UserDefaults(suiteName: name)`
instead of the bundle's domain, AND the instance counts whatever its socket or home.

- One switch does both on purpose: counting cannot be turned on in a proof instance without
  also moving the state out of the real domain.
- The name must start with `framejob.` (`proof_defaults.PREFIXES`, so `remove_domain` and the
  sweep own it). Any other value, or a suite that cannot be made, is named on stderr and
  ignored whole: the instance stays scratch (`DevAppearance.swift`'s precedent).
- `static let devSuiteKey = "RCDevTipsSuite"`. `TipsInstance.isPersons` is
  `devStore != nil || counts(…)`; `TipsAsk.shared` is over `devStore ?? .standard`.
- Not in Distribution (compiled out). No `dist_check` row: the D44/D45 pair exists for a
  switch that widens a fetch, and the other two dozen `-RCDev` switches have none.
- Why a switch at all (TIP-7 said none): a counted agent export on the live app, with the
  window really ordered and the next call really answered, cannot be seen without writing some
  defaults domain, and it must not be the bundle's.

### 5. The proof (`tools/proof/tips_proof.py`, `tools/proof/tips_probe.swift`)

Probe rows (the probe is built without the dev-tools flag, as now):

- **I1** `counts` on literal environments: neither variable and a bundle id true; a socket
  path false; an empty socket value true.
- **I2** `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` set false; empty true.
- **I3** no bundle id false; and the probe's own `TipsInstance.isPersons` is false.
- **W3** reworded: job A is "a job nobody followed", no longer "the agent's".
- **W4, the agent's door, counted.** `AgentServer.shared.exportProject(_:tips:)` on an
  in-process document, with `TipsDoors(ask:dialog:queue: .shared, counts: { true })` on the
  one-export-short state. The document gets a `fileURL` in the scratch folder and is added to
  `NSDocumentController`, and the call names it by `project`, so `target` is deterministic.
  Checks: the answer carries an `export_id`; the job reaches `completed`; exports 5 from 4;
  orders `["front"]`; last asked is the clock; `NSApp.modalWindow` is nil and the watchdog saw
  no modal session; `exportStatus` answers `done` afterwards; a second `export` completes,
  exports 6, orders unchanged.
- **W5, the queue door in a scratch instance.** The same handler with `counts: { false }`:
  the export completes, the store is byte-for-byte what it was, nothing is ordered.
- **W6, the Export… door in a scratch instance.** `beginExport(…, tips:)` with
  `counts: { false }`, a success and Close: the same.
- **A modal watchdog**, installed at the probe's start: a repeating timer in the common modes
  that counts a modal session and aborts it, so a mutant that blocks fails a row instead of
  hanging the run. W4's door orders its dialog as C1's does (moved off every display first).

Text row **T1**: `.follow(queueJob:` is called exactly twice, once in
`EditorViewController+Export.swift` and once in `AgentServer+Export.swift`; `TipsDoors` is
named in those two and its own file alone; the other three facts stand; `RCDevTipsSuite`
appears in `Tips.swift` alone.

Live rows (`mcp.launch`, each instance stopped by its own pid):

- **L2** kept, reworded as the proof-instance row: an agent `export` reaches `done`, no
  window is titled "Tips", `mcp.defaults_moved` is empty.
- **L4, counted, with an editor window.** A suite `framejob.tips-proof.<pid>.a` seeded with
  `defaults write` (4 exports, a first export 40 days back; `proof_defaults.read_env()`),

## Proof

| Item | Check | Seen failing by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 agent exports count | W4 (5 from 4, first-export logic through `countExport`, A1 unchanged); L4 and L5 read 5 in the suite | `agent-unfollowed` restores today's behaviour: W4 and T1 fail |
| 2 the window opens | W4 orders `["front"]`; L4 and L5 list a visible "Tips" window | `agent-unfollowed` (W4), `auto-takes-key` (W4) |
| 2 it blocks nothing | W4: no modal session, `exportStatus` and a second export answer; L4: `get_project`, `perform_menu_item` and a second export answer | `ask-runs-modal`: W4 |
| 3 the spec | `spec_index_proof.py` in `make test` (rows, Lines) | its existing failure on a stale Lines cell |
| 4 proof instances | I1, I2, I3; W5, W6; L2 on a real proof instance | `socket-ignored`, `home-ignored`, `bundle-ignored`, `queue-ignores-instance`, `card-ignores-instance` |

Order of work: the spec; the code with `make typecheck` in the loop; `tips_proof.py
--no-live`; `make app-debug` and the full proof on Debug; the eighteen mutants once (probe
rebuilds, no app); `make gate` once; then the full proof with `RC_PROOF_APP=release`. A
mutant never runs an L row, so no mutant can write the owner's domain. `assistant_lane_proof.py`
and `mutant_anchors.py` run inside the gate's `make test`; `screens.py` P2 is run by its
narrowest selection.

## Risks

- **The suite under `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`.** The live instances run under a scratch home
  (`tips_proof.py:343-345`). The B83/B84 measurements say no environment moves `UserDefaults`
  for the bundle's domain; a named suite is assumed to behave the same. L4 has its own
  control: if the app does not see the seed, it counts 1 and never asks, and the row says so.
  If that happens the fix is in the proof (launch L4 and L5 without the scratch home), not in
  the app.
- **The modal watchdog under `ask-runs-modal`.** If a modal session cannot be aborted from a
  timer in a `.prohibited` probe, the mutant ends as "control could not be performed" (exit
  2), which the mutant run shows. The mutant may also flash the dialog on screen for a moment;
  the off-display order in W4's door is there to prevent it.
- **The owner's real count now moves with agent use**, including any session whose MCP
  configuration points at the owner's default socket (a Claude Code session with the
  `framejob` server). That is the request. Nothing a proof launches is such an instance.
- **A person's test copy** (their own `RC_AGENT_SOCKET`) stops counting card exports too. See
  Owner choices.
- **In-process callers of `exportProject`.** `assistant_lane_probe.swift` reaches
  `TipsDoors.shared` once this lands; the bundle guard makes that a no-op, and I3 holds the
  guard. Without it a completed in-process export would write `FrameJobTipsExports` into the
  probe's own domain and make `proof_defaults`' sweep report it busy.
- **Callers.** `beginExport(…, tips:)` and `enqueueExport` are unchanged. `TipsDoors.init`
  gains a defaulted parameter; the probe's three existing constructions pass `counts: { true }`.
- **Concurrency.** Everything stays on main: `follow` is called inside `exportProject`'s
  existing main block, and the follower settles inside the queue's post as it does today.
- **Persisted data.** No key is added or renamed; no project format change.
- **Run time.** Eighteen probe rebuilds, and two more live instances (four in all).

## Owner choices

1. **A test copy counts nothing, from any door.** With `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` (or a relocated
   home) set, even a person's own Export… in that copy is not counted. The alternative is to
   gate only the agent's door. Recommended, and planned: gate both, so the rule is one
   sentence about the instance and a future dev switch that answers the save panel cannot
   start writing the owner's keys from a proof.
2. **One dev switch for the proof**, reversing TIP-7's "no `-RCDev` switch". The alternative
   is probe rows only, with no live row that sees a counted agent export or the window.
   Recommended, and planned: the switch, because the request asks to verify the window from
   the agent's door on the running app.

## Not doing

- **No change to the schedule, the window, the toolbar button or Settings' pane.** None is
  needed.
- **No origin on queue jobs and no change to `ExportQueueController`.** The follower by id
  already serves both doors.
- **No edit to `mcp.py`, `proof_app.py`, the harness or any other proof's launch.** The rule
  reads what they already set.
- **No guard on `noteTipPageOpened`.** It is a person's press of Leave a Tip, which no tool
  can make.
- **No forced app activation state in the live rows.** A proof cannot make Frame Job inactive
  without taking the owner's focus; CH-10 is the person's check.
- **No `CLAUDE.md` edit.** Owed to the orchestrator:
  - `app/CLAUDE.md`, the Tips entry: `TipsDoors` is called from
    `EditorViewController+Export.swift` AND `AgentServer+Export.swift`; "nothing off a
    person's door writes a key" becomes "nothing in a scratch instance writes a key (TIP-8)";
    `TipsInstance` and `-RCDevTipsSuite` named; TIP-1…TIP-8.
  - Root `CLAUDE.md`, "Verifying a build": `-RCDevTipsSuite <name>` added to the dev-only
    launch defaults (spec §11 TIP-7).

systemPrompt:
You are the only independent check on a change that one agent both designs and builds. Your prompt says which job you are doing. You get one round. You never edit code; Write is for your output file only, and Bash is for read-only inspection (`git diff`, `git log`, `rg`, reading files).

Never search the filesystem outside the repo and the handoff dir.

What counts, in both jobs: a defect you can show. Each finding needs evidence, a `file:line` or a concrete scenario with the inputs and the wrong result. Leave out style, naming, wording, "consider also", speculative future needs, and a different overall approach unless the current one is demonstrably broken. Finding nothing is a good outcome; say so in one line. Do not manufacture findings.

## Plan challenge: write `02-objections.md`

Read `request.md` and `01-plan.md`. Then read the code yourself: the files the plan names, and their callers and neighbours where the plan's claims depend on them. Do not take the plan's "What is true now" on trust; check it.

Look for:

- a claim about the code that is false or has moved
- a case the change gets wrong: an input, an ordering, a race, a caller the plan did not name
- a proof that would pass without the change, or that was never going to be seen failing
- an item of the request the plan drops or narrows without saying so
- work the request did not ask for
- a conflict with a rule or recorded decision of the repo

Write each objection as: **Claim** (one or two sentences), **Evidence**, **Suggested change** (one sentence). Order them by how much damage each would do. End with `verdict: proceed` or `verdict: revise`.

## Diff read: write `04-diff-read.md`

Read `request.md` and the diff you are given. Read the changed files and what calls them. Do NOT read the plan or the build notes until you have formed your findings: you are checking the code, not whether it matches a document. After that, read the build notes once, only to drop a finding they already answer with evidence.

Look for what breaks: wrong results, crashes, races, lost data, a caller left behind, a check that cannot fail, a document the change made false.

Write each finding as: severity (`blocker`: breaks or is wrong today; `should-fix`: a real defect that will not bite today; `nit`: anything else), **Where** (`file:line`), **What**, **Fix**, one line each. End with `verdict: pass` (no blocker and no should-fix) or `verdict: fix-required`.

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

49	  nothing completes, but the door is reachable.

51	  (`UISnapshot.swift:130-137`, `:168-181`), so a live row can see the Tips window without a
52	  new tool. `perform_menu_item` refuses while an app-modal window is up
53	  (`AgentServer+MenuItem.swift:194-198`), so it is a direct read of "modal to nothing".
54	- **The request's premise about launch paths is slightly off.** The offscreen harness and the
55	  probes are bare executables that bind no socket and are not "launched" through
56	  `proof_app.py`; the mechanism below covers them by what they are, not by a launcher change.
57	  `mcp.py` and `proof_app.py` need no edit.
58	
59	## Change
60	
61	### 0. Spec, before any code (`designs/spec/11-decisions/tips.md`, its `README.md`, `designs/spec/README.md`)
62	
63	- **TIP-4, rewritten in place**, opening "(amended 2026-11-14, the owner: 'Exports over the

75	- **TIP-7**: amended. The feature has ONE dev switch, `-RCDevTipsSuite <name>` (below), and

99	  variable set in `bounded.child_env`) is something an own-`Popen` proof forgets, and there

101	  instance to talk to. `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` closes the one other route to a non-owner socket
102	  (the default path under a scratch home). The bundle condition covers probes and the
103	  harness, which call app code in a bare executable. None is something an MCP client sets by
104	  accident: a client's configuration reaches the helper, and the helper passes the variable to
105	  the app only for a scratch socket (`mcp-proxy/src/launch.rs`, `open_arguments`).

107	  copy on its own socket is not counted".

181	
182	- **L2** kept, reworded as the proof-instance row: an agent `export` reaches `done`, no

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Tips (spec §11 TIP-1…TIP-7): what the dialog links to, when Frame Job asks
4	/// by itself, and what it remembers. Foundation only, so a probe can run the
5	/// rule against a clock of its own and the AppKit-free export queue can be
6	/// followed from here. The dialog is `TipsWindowController.swift`, the
7	/// editor's button `TipsToolbarButton.swift`, Settings' pane
8	/// `TipsSettingsPane.swift`.
9	
10	/// The one address "Leave a Tip" opens (TIP-1). The page is the owner's.
11	enum TipsLink {
12	    static let url = "https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/"
13	}
14	
15	/// What the schedule is decided from: the stored state, read at one moment.
16	struct TipsState: Equatable {
17	    /// When the first counted export succeeded; nil before one has.
18	    var firstExport: Date?
19	    /// How many exports a person confirmed in the export card have succeeded.
20	    var exports = 0
21	    /// When the automatic ask was last shown, or "Leave a Tip" last pressed.
22	    var lastAsked: Date?
23	    /// Settings ▸ Tips' toggle.
24	    var enabled = true
25	}
26	
27	/// When the automatic ask is due (TIP-3). Pure: the state, a moment and a
28	/// calendar in, a Bool out.
29	enum TipsSchedule {
30	    static let firstAskDays = 30
31	    static let firstAskExports = 5
32	    static let skipMonths = 6
33	
34	    /// The Gregorian calendar in the Mac's time zone as it is now, whatever
35	    /// calendar the person's Mac shows: "December" is its month 12.
36	    static func localCalendar() -> Calendar {
37	        var calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)
38	        calendar.timeZone = TimeZone.current
39	        return calendar
40	    }
41	
42	    /// Off is never due. The first ask waits for `firstAskExports` exports
43	    /// and `firstAskDays` days since the first of them. After an ask, only a
44	    /// December is due, and not one whose 1 December 00:00 is less than
45	    /// `skipMonths` calendar months after the last ask.
46	    static func isDue(_ state: TipsState, now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Bool {
47	        guard state.enabled else { return false }
48	        guard let first = state.firstExport else { return false }
49	        guard state.exports >= firstAskExports else { return false }
50	        guard now.timeIntervalSince(first) >= Double(firstAskDays) * 86_400 else { return false }
51	        guard let last = state.lastAsked else { return true }
52	        guard calendar.component(.month, from: now) == 12 else { return false }
53	        let year = calendar.component(.year, from: now)
54	        guard
55	            let december = calendar.date(from: DateComponents(year: year, month: 12, day: 1)),
56	            let earliest = calendar.date(byAdding: .month, value: skipMonths, to: last)
57	        else { return false }
58	        return earliest <= december
59	    }
60	}
61	
62	/// Settings ▸ Tips' toggle (TIP-5, TIP-6): on shows the editor's Tips button
63	/// and lets the automatic ask happen.
64	enum TipsSettings {
65	    /// Bool; absent = true.
66	    static let enabledKey = "FrameJobTips"
67	
68	    /// Posted after the toggle is written, so every editor's Tips button
69	    /// follows it at once.
70	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name("FrameJobTipsSettingsDidChange")
71	
72	    static func isEnabled(in defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) -> Bool {
73	        defaults.object(forKey: enabledKey) == nil ? true : defaults.bool(forKey: enabledKey)
74	    }
75	
76	    /// Writes the toggle and posts `didChangeNotification`.
77	    static func setEnabled(_ enabled: Bool, in defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) {
78	        defaults.set(enabled, forKey: enabledKey)
79	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: didChangeNotification, object: nil)
80	    }
81	}
82	
83	/// The stored state and its three writers (TIP-5). Every writer is reached
84	/// only from a person's door: an export confirmed in the export card, or the
85	/// dialog's "Leave a Tip". Main thread.
86	final class TipsAsk {
87	    /// Int; absent = 0.
88	    static let exportsKey = "FrameJobTipsExports"
89	    /// A date, stamped by the first counted export and never again.
90	    static let firstExportKey = "FrameJobTipsFirstExport"
91	    /// A date: the last automatic ask, or the last press of "Leave a Tip".
92	    static let lastAskedKey = "FrameJobTipsLastAsked"
93	
94	    /// The app's own, over the bundle's defaults and the real clock.
95	    static let shared = TipsAsk()
96	
97	    private let defaults: UserDefaults
98	    private let now: () -> Date
99	    private let calendar: () -> Calendar
100	
101	    init(
102	        defaults: UserDefaults = .standard, now: @escaping () -> Date = { Date() },
103	        calendar: @escaping () -> Calendar = { TipsSchedule.localCalendar() }
104	    ) {
105	        self.defaults = defaults
106	        self.now = now
107	        self.calendar = calendar
108	    }
109	
110	    var state: TipsState {
111	        TipsState(
112	            firstExport: defaults.object(forKey: Self.firstExportKey) as? Date,
113	            exports: defaults.integer(forKey: Self.exportsKey),
114	            lastAsked: defaults.object(forKey: Self.lastAskedKey) as? Date,
115	            enabled: TipsSettings.isEnabled(in: defaults))
116	    }
117	
118	    /// One more export a person confirmed has succeeded. Counts whatever the
119	    /// toggle says.
120	    func countExport() {
121	        let state = self.state
122	        defaults.set(state.exports + 1, forKey: Self.exportsKey)
123	        if state.firstExport == nil { defaults.set(now(), forKey: Self.firstExportKey) }
124	    }
125	
126	    /// True when the automatic ask is due now, and then it is recorded as
127	    /// asked, so the caller shows the dialog and a second call answers false.
128	    func takeAsk() -> Bool {
129	        let moment = now()
130	        guard TipsSchedule.isDue(state, now: moment, calendar: calendar()) else { return false }
131	        defaults.set(moment, forKey: Self.lastAskedKey)
132	        return true
133	    }
134	
135	    /// "Leave a Tip" was pressed, from any door: that is an ask too.
136	    func noteTipPageOpened() {
137	        defaults.set(now(), forKey: Self.lastAskedKey)
138	    }
139	}
140	
141	/// Which export queue jobs a person started (Add to Queue), followed by id as
142	/// `AgentExports` follows the agent's, so the queue's jobs carry no origin
143	/// (TIP-4). `settle()` runs on every change of the queue.
144	final class TipsQueueFollower {
145	    private let state: (UInt64) -> ExportQueueController.State?
146	    private let completed: () -> Void
147	    private(set) var followed: Set<UInt64> = []
148	
149	    init(state: @escaping (UInt64) -> ExportQueueController.State?, completed: @escaping () -> Void)
150	    {
151	        self.state = state
152	        self.completed = completed
153	    }
154	
155	    func follow(_ id: UInt64) {
156	        followed.insert(id)
157	        settle()
158	    }
159	
160	    /// A followed job that completed calls `completed` once and is dropped;
161	    /// one cancelled, failed or gone from the list is dropped; one waiting or
162	    /// running stays.
163	    func settle() {
164	        for id in followed.sorted() {
165	            switch state(id) {
166	            case .completed:
167	                followed.remove(id)
168	                completed()
169	            case .cancelled, .failed, nil:
170	                followed.remove(id)
171	            case .waiting, .running:
172	                break
173	            }
174	        }
175	    }
176	}

1	import AppKit
2	
3	/// The Tips dialog (spec §11 TIP-1, TIP-2): who a tip funds, "Leave a Tip"
4	/// and "Not Now".
5	///
6	/// **A window and not a sheet, deliberately.** It has three doors — the
7	/// editor's Tips button, Settings' Tips button and the automatic ask — and
8	/// two of them have no document to hold a sheet. It is modal to nothing, so
9	/// no window and no tool call ever waits on it. `SettingsWindowController`'s
10	/// mould: one instance, not released when closed, no frame autosave name.
11	/// It is built from the sheets' own pieces so it reads as one of them, and
12	/// it is left out of the Window menu because both buttons reopen it.
13	///
14	/// **Two ways to show it.** `show()` is a person's press: key and front, and
15	/// it writes nothing. `showAutomatic()` is the ask Frame Job makes by itself
16	/// (TIP-4): front WITHOUT key, so a Return typed into the editor can never
17	/// press "Leave a Tip". The two order calls are closures because a probe's
18	/// window is never key and could not tell the two apart otherwise.
19	///
20	/// **What "Leave a Tip" does.** Opens `TipsLink.url` in the browser, records
21	/// the press as an ask (TIP-5) and closes. Nothing here knows whether anyone
22	/// tipped.
23	final class TipsWindowController: NSWindowController {
24	    /// The app's one Tips dialog. A probe builds its own.
25	    static let shared = TipsWindowController()
26	
27	    static let windowTitle = "Tips"
28	    static let heading = "Frame Job is free and open source"
29	    static let body =
30	        "Frame Job is made by one developer. It is free to use and its source is open. If it "
31	        + "is useful to you, a tip helps pay for the time to keep working on it. Tips are "
32	        + "voluntary, and nothing in Frame Job is locked without one."
33	    static let hint = "You can turn this reminder off in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Tips."
34	    static let notNowTitle = "Not Now"
35	    static let tipTitle = "Leave a Tip"
36	
37	    private let ask: TipsAsk
38	    private let open: (URL) -> Void
39	    private let orderKey: (NSWindow) -> Void
40	    private let orderFront: (NSWindow) -> Void
41	
42	    private(set) var notNowButton: NSButton!
43	    private(set) var tipButton: NSButton!
44	
45	    init(
46	        ask: TipsAsk = .shared,
47	        open: @escaping (URL) -> Void = { NSWorkspace.shared.open($0) },
48	        orderKey: @escaping (NSWindow) -> Void = { $0.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil) },
49	        orderFront: @escaping (NSWindow) -> Void = { $0.orderFront(nil) }
50	    ) {
51	        self.ask = ask
52	        self.open = open
53	        self.orderKey = orderKey
54	        self.orderFront = orderFront
55	        let window = NSWindow(
56	            contentRect: NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: sheetWidth, height: 240),
57	            styleMask: [.titled, .closable], backing: .buffered, defer: false)
58	        window.title = Self.windowTitle
59	        window.isReleasedWhenClosed = false
60	        window.isExcludedFromWindowsMenu = true
61	        super.init(window: window)
62	        let content = buildContent()
63	        window.contentView = content
64	        window.setContentSize(content.fittingSize)
65	        window.center()
66	        applyBackground()
67	    }
68	
69	    @available(*, unavailable)
70	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
71	        fatalError("TipsWindowController does not support NSCoder")
72	    }
73	
74	    private func buildContent() -> NSView {
75	        let width = sheetWidth - sheetInset * 2
76	        let bodyLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: Self.body)
77	        bodyLabel.font = DS.sans(13)
78	        bodyLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
79	        bodyLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = width
80	        bodyLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tips.body")
81	
82	        let hintLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: Self.hint)
83	        hintLabel.font = DS.sans(12)
84	        hintLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
85	        hintLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = width
86	        hintLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tips.hint")
87	
88	        notNowButton = StickerButton(
89	            title: Self.notNowTitle, style: .secondary, target: self,
90	            action: #selector(notNowClicked(_:)))
91	        notNowButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tips.notnow")
92	        tipButton = StickerButton(
93	            title: Self.tipTitle, style: .primary, target: self,
94	            action: #selector(tipClicked(_:)))
95	        tipButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tips.tip")
96	
97	        return makeSheetView(
98	            title: Self.heading, content: sheetColumn([bodyLabel, hintLabel]),
99	            buttonRow: makeButtonRow(cancel: notNowButton, apply: tipButton))
100	    }
101	
102	    private func applyBackground() {
103	        window?.backgroundColor = DS.chromeBackground
104	        window?.contentView?.layer?.backgroundColor = DS.chromeBackground.cgColor
105	    }
106	
107	    // MARK: - Showing
108	
109	    /// A person's press of a Tips button: key and front. Writes nothing.
110	    func show() {
111	        guard let window else { return }
112	        applyBackground()
113	        orderKey(window)
114	    }
115	
116	    /// The ask Frame Job makes by itself: front, never key (TIP-4).
117	    func showAutomatic() {
118	        guard let window else { return }
119	        applyBackground()
120	        orderFront(window)
121	    }
122	
123	    // MARK: - Buttons
124	
125	    @objc func notNowClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
126	        close()
127	    }
128	
129	    @objc func tipClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
130	        if let url = URL(string: TipsLink.url) { open(url) }
131	        ask.noteTipPageOpened()
132	        close()
133	    }
134	}
135	
136	// MARK: - The export doors
137	
138	/// The two places a person's export reaches Tips (TIP-4): the Export… sheet's
139	/// success and an Add to Queue job. `EditorViewController+Export.swift` is
140	/// the only caller; the agent's `export` never comes here. The ask, the
141	/// dialog and the queue are parameters so a probe runs both doors on its own.
142	/// Main thread.
143	final class TipsDoors {
144	    static let shared = TipsDoors()
145	
146	    private let ask: TipsAsk
147	    private let dialog: () -> TipsWindowController
148	    private let queue: ExportQueueController
149	    private var follower: TipsQueueFollower?
150	    private var queueObserver: NSObjectProtocol?
151	    /// The result sheets still up after a counted success, each waiting for
152	    /// its window's sheet to end.
153	    private var sheetEnds: [TipsSheetEnd] = []
154	
155	    init(
156	        ask: TipsAsk = .shared,
157	        dialog: @escaping () -> TipsWindowController = { TipsWindowController.shared },
158	        queue: ExportQueueController = .shared
159	    ) {
160	        self.ask = ask
161	        self.dialog = dialog
162	        self.queue = queue
163	    }
164	
165	    deinit {
166	        if let queueObserver { NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(queueObserver) }
167	    }
168	
169	    /// An Export… the person confirmed has succeeded: counted now. The ask
170	    /// waits until `window`'s sheet — the export's own result panel — ends,
171	    /// and one main-queue turn more so the sheet has left; with no sheet
172	    /// attached it is asked at once.
173	    func exportSucceeded(sheetOn window: NSWindow?) {
174	        ask.countExport()
175	        guard let window, window.attachedSheet != nil else {
176	            askIfDue()
177	            return
178	        }
179	        sheetEnds.append(
180	            TipsSheetEnd(window: window) { [weak self] watch in
181	                guard let self else { return }
182	                self.sheetEnds.removeAll { $0 === watch }
183	                self.askIfDue()
184	            })
185	    }
186	
187	    /// An Add to Queue job the person confirmed: followed to its end by id.
188	    /// A completion counts and asks; a cancel or a failure does neither.
189	    func follow(queueJob id: UInt64) {
190	        if follower == nil {
191	            follower = TipsQueueFollower(
192	                state: { [queue] in queue.job($0)?.state },
193	                completed: { [weak self] in
194	                    self?.ask.countExport()
195	                    self?.askIfDue()
196	                })
197	            queueObserver = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
198	                forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification, object: queue, queue: nil
199	            ) { [weak self] _ in self?.follower?.settle() }
200	        }
201	        follower?.follow(id)
202	    }
203	
204	    /// Shows the dialog when the schedule says so, recording the ask at the
205	    /// moment it is shown.
206	    private func askIfDue() {
207	        guard ask.takeAsk() else { return }
208	        dialog().showAutomatic()
209	    }
210	}
211	
212	/// One wait for a window's sheet to end, then one main-queue turn.
213	private final class TipsSheetEnd: NSObject {
214	    private let then: (TipsSheetEnd) -> Void
215	
216	    init(window: NSWindow, then: @escaping (TipsSheetEnd) -> Void) {
217	        self.then = then
218	        super.init()
219	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
220	            self, selector: #selector(ended(_:)), name: NSWindow.didEndSheetNotification,
221	            object: window)
222	    }
223	
224	    @objc private func ended(_ note: Notification) {
225	        NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(self)
226	        DispatchQueue.main.async { self.then(self) }
227	    }
228	}
229	
230	// MARK: - The command
231	
232	/// The command half, at the foot of the file that owns the feature
233	/// (`SettingsWindowController.swift`'s precedent): a nil-target selector, so
234	/// the editor's Tips button resolves it through the responder chain.
235	extension AppDelegate {
236	    @objc func showTips(_ sender: Any?) {
237	        TipsWindowController.shared.show()
238	    }
239	}

1	import AppKit
2	
3	extension AgentServer {
4	
5	    // MARK: - Export
6	
7	    /// `export` — ⌘E (`EditorViewController.exportProjectCommand` and
8	    /// `ExportSheetController`). The preset names the ENCODING — a container
9	    /// and a codec, nothing about size — and the size is the sheet's separate
10	    /// choice, in the Size popup's own vocabulary and defaulting as the popup
11	    /// does to its first row: the document's size, or an image format's cap.
12	    /// The CORE resolves both into concrete settings (`rc_export_settings`)
13	    /// that go to the same `Exporter.export` the sheet uses: there is exactly
14	    /// one writer, so an agent export and a menu export cannot disagree.
15	    ///
16	    /// Answers AT ONCE (spec §11 #326): every refusal is made here, before
17	    /// anything is queued — the arguments, the core's settings, the folder,
18	    /// the graphics gate, and the frame limit and same-shape rule
19	    /// (`Exporter.settingsRefusal`, #470) — and the export is then a job in the Export
20	    /// Queue, exactly as the sheet's Add to Queue makes one, answered as
21	    /// `{export_id, path, status}`. `export_status` follows the job and
22	    /// `cancel_export` stops it (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`); a failure
23	    /// while writing comes back from there. The queue window is not shown.
24	    ///
25	    /// One argument is NOT a setting and never reaches the core:
26	    /// `burn_in_timecode` is a recipe option (`RecipeOptions`), read below
27	    /// beside the overrides it deliberately does not join.
28	    ///
29	    /// The finished job's answer carries the sound the file actually holds —
30	    /// its integrated loudness and true peak, measured on the way through —
31	    /// for every format that has any, whether `loudness_lufs` was asked for
32	    /// or not, and, with `stems` (the sheet's Stems popup, spec §11 AU-108),
33	    /// each stem file beside the mix.
34	    func exportProject(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
35	        // The clock `export_status`'s `elapsed` runs on, read before any check.
36	        let started = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
37	        let presetID = try requiredString(a, "preset")
38	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
39	        let wholeProject = (try stringArg(a, "range") ?? "project").lowercased()
40	        guard ["project", "in_out"].contains(wholeProject) else {
41	            throw ToolError(
42	                message: "range must be \"project\" (the whole timeline) or \"in_out\" "
43	                    + "(the in/out range set_range set), not \"\(wholeProject)\".")
44	        }
45	        // The export sheet's burn-in checkbox — and read HERE rather than
46	        // into `overrides` below, which is the whole of the decision. A
47	        // recipe option changes the PICTURE, so it travels with the
48	        // description of the picture: `export_overrides.rs` ignores a key it
49	        // does not know, on purpose, so a `burn_in_timecode` posted through
50	        // `rc_export_settings` would vanish without a word and this tool
51	        // would report success on an un-burnt file. It goes to `Exporter`
52	        // beside the settings instead (`RecipeOptions`, `Exporter.export`),
53	        // which is also what reaches GIF and APNG — those never go through
54	        // `ExportWriter` at all.
55	        let options = RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: try boolArg(a, "burn_in_timecode") ?? false)
56	        let prepared = try onMain {
57	            () throws -> (ProjectDocument, ReelProject, [UInt32: URL], ExportSettings, GraphicSet?)
58	            in
59	            let document = try self.target(a)
60	            guard document.project.duration > 0 else {
61	                throw ToolError(message: "There is nothing on the timeline to export.")
62	            }
63	            let settings = try self.exportSettings(
64	                a, on: document, preset: presetID, range: wholeProject)
65	            return (
66	                document, document.project, document.mediaURLs(), settings,
67	                GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)
68	            )
69	        }
70	        let (document, project, urls, settings, graphics) = prepared
71	        let url = try Self.requireFolder(
72	            of: Self.destinationURL(path, extension: Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings)))
73	
74	        // The graphics gate, here rather than only in the writer: a module
75	        // that does not compile refuses the CALL, so nothing is queued that
76	        // could only fail (`Exporter.graphicsRefusal`, the writer's own gate).
77	        if let refusal = Exporter.graphicsRefusal(
78	            project: project, settings: settings, graphics: graphics)
79	        {
80	            throw ToolError(message: refusal.localizedDescription)
81	        }
82	        // The same, for the two rules the sheet shows in its readout (#470).
83	        if let refusal = Exporter.settingsRefusal(settings, project: project) {
84	            throw ToolError(message: refusal.localizedDescription)
85	        }
86	        let (id, status) = onMain { () -> (UInt64, String) in

atexit.register(_defaults_at_exit)


def target(argv, index=1, env_fallback=True):
    """`argv[index]`, else `$RC_AGENT_SOCKET`; failing both, a usage exit."""
    if len(argv) > index and argv[index]:
        return argv[index]
    if env_fallback and os.environ.get("RC_AGENT_SOCKET"):
        return os.environ["RC_AGENT_SOCKET"]
    script = os.path.basename(argv[0]) if argv else "the proof"
    raise SystemExit(
        f"usage: pass the running instance's socket path (python3 {script} <dir>/agent.sock), "
        "the RC_AGENT_SOCKET it was launched with" + ("" if not env_fallback else
                                                     ", or set RC_AGENT_SOCKET"))


# ---- the launcher ----------------------------------------------------------------

class Launched:
    """One instance `launch` started: its child, socket, log and client."""

    def __init__(self, child, socket_path, log_path, client):
        self.child = child
        self.socket_path = socket_path
        self.log_path = log_path
        self.client = client

    def stop(self, grace=30):
        """Terminates this child alone, then kills it after `grace`."""
        if self.child is None or self.child.poll() is not None:
            return
        self.child.terminate()
        try:
            self.child.wait(timeout=grace)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            self.child.kill()
            self.child.wait()


def _child_env():
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                                    "graphics_spike"))
    import bounded  # noqa: E402

    return bounded.child_env()


def launch(binary, arguments=(), env=None, socket_path=None, log_path=None, seconds=60,
           timeout=600):
    """Starts `binary -ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES *arguments` on a
    scratch socket (or `socket_path`), in its own session, logging to
    `log_path` (else beside the socket), and waits up to `seconds` for its
    listening line. `client` is an `MCP` with `timeout`, or None when the
    instance did not come up. A built product older than its inputs is
    refused first (`proof_app.StaleApp`), and so is a bare negative number
    among `arguments` (`proof_app.launch_arguments`, a `ValueError`, #404);
    nothing is started."""
    arguments = proof_app.launch_arguments(arguments)
    proof_app.require_fresh(binary)
    socket_path = str(socket_path or scratch_socket())
    log_path = str(log_path or log_beside(socket_path))
    environment = dict(env) if env is not None else _child_env()
    environment["RC_AGENT_SOCKET"] = socket_path
    offset = os.path.getsize(log_path) if os.path.exists(log_path) else 0
    earlier = _GUARDED.pop(socket_path, None)
    if earlier is not None and earlier["own"]:
        _finish(socket_path, earlier)      # a relaunch on the same socket loses nothing
    _record(socket_path, proof_defaults.bundle_domain(binary) or proof_defaults.APP_DOMAIN)
    with open(log_path, "ab") as out:
        child = subprocess.Popen(
            [str(binary), "-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState", "YES", *arguments],
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            start_new_session=True, env=environment)
    _own(socket_path, child.pid)
    client = None
    if wait_listening(log_path, socket_path, child=child, seconds=seconds, offset=offset):
        try:
            client = MCP(socket_path, timeout=timeout)
        except proof_app.StaleApp:
            Launched(child, socket_path, log_path, None).stop()
            raise
    return Launched(child, socket_path, log_path, client)

551	def target(argv, index=1, env_fallback=True):
552	    """`argv[index]`, else `$RC_AGENT_SOCKET`; failing both, a usage exit."""
553	    if len(argv) > index and argv[index]:
554	        return argv[index]
555	    if env_fallback and os.environ.get("RC_AGENT_SOCKET"):
556	        return os.environ["RC_AGENT_SOCKET"]
557	    script = os.path.basename(argv[0]) if argv else "the proof"
558	    raise SystemExit(
559	        f"usage: pass the running instance's socket path (python3 {script} <dir>/agent.sock), "
560	        "the RC_AGENT_SOCKET it was launched with" + ("" if not env_fallback else
561	                                                     ", or set RC_AGENT_SOCKET"))
562

564	# ---- the launcher ----------------------------------------------------------------
565	
566	class Launched:
567	    """One instance `launch` started: its child, socket, log and client."""
568	
569	    def __init__(self, child, socket_path, log_path, client):
570	        self.child = child
571	        self.socket_path = socket_path
572	        self.log_path = log_path
573	        self.client = client
574	
575	    def stop(self, grace=30):
576	        """Terminates this child alone, then kills it after `grace`."""
577	        if self.child is None or self.child.poll() is not None:
578	            return
579	        self.child.terminate()
580	        try:
581	            self.child.wait(timeout=grace)
582	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
583	            self.child.kill()
584	            self.child.wait()

595	def launch(binary, arguments=(), env=None, socket_path=None, log_path=None, seconds=60,
596	           timeout=600):
597	    """Starts `binary -ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES *arguments` on a
598	    scratch socket (or `socket_path`), in its own session, logging to
599	    `log_path` (else beside the socket), and waits up to `seconds` for its
600	    listening line. `client` is an `MCP` with `timeout`, or None when the
601	    instance did not come up. A built product older than its inputs is
602	    refused first (`proof_app.StaleApp`), and so is a bare negative number
603	    among `arguments` (`proof_app.launch_arguments`, a `ValueError`, #404);
604	    nothing is started."""
605	    arguments = proof_app.launch_arguments(arguments)
606	    proof_app.require_fresh(binary)
607	    socket_path = str(socket_path or scratch_socket())
608	    log_path = str(log_path or log_beside(socket_path))
609	    environment = dict(env) if env is not None else _child_env()
610	    environment["RC_AGENT_SOCKET"] = socket_path
611	    offset = os.path.getsize(log_path) if os.path.exists(log_path) else 0
612	    earlier = _GUARDED.pop(socket_path, None)
613	    if earlier is not None and earlier["own"]:
614	        _finish(socket_path, earlier)      # a relaunch on the same socket loses nothing
615	    _record(socket_path, proof_defaults.bundle_domain(binary) or proof_defaults.APP_DOMAIN)
616	    with open(log_path, "ab") as out:
617	        child = subprocess.Popen(
618	            [str(binary), "-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState", "YES", *arguments],
619	            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
620	            start_new_session=True, env=environment)
621	    _own(socket_path, child.pid)
622	    client = None
623	    if wait_listening(log_path, socket_path, child=child, seconds=seconds, offset=offset):
624	        try:
625	            client = MCP(socket_path, timeout=timeout)
626	        except proof_app.StaleApp:
627	            Launched(child, socket_path, log_path, None).stop()
628	            raise
629	    return Launched(child, socket_path, log_path, client)
