#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Road map 2, phase 8 (Viewing and finding) — the OFFSCREEN half of the proof.

**Phase 8 is three features and the harness can photograph one of them**, which
is why this script is mostly PROBES. Preview Quality scales the PLAYER's video
composition — the preview well renders black offscreen because a Metal layer
has no drawable there, so no render at any size can show the difference.
Preview Window is a SECOND window, and the harness captures the editor's
content view. The Media tab's find band is the one thing that is drawn inside
that view, and section 7 photographs it.

**Section 9 is the exception, and it is the phase's own defect made
measurable.** The harness cannot photograph a preview, but a PROBE can render
one: `AVAssetImageGenerator` over a composition built exactly as `Playback`
builds it, with `renderSize` scaled by `Playback.previewComposition` itself,
answers a CGImage at 1920 x 1080, 960 x 540 and 480 x 270 with no window and no
drawable anywhere. That is how the reduced sizes came to be looked at at all —
and what it showed was that `[[position]]` is in DESTINATION pixels while three
fragment stages took it for canvas pixels, which was true only while
`renderSize` was always the canvas. Section 9 is that reading, kept.

So the instrument is `phase6_chrome.py`'s and `phase7_chrome.py`'s: a
`main.swift` of this script's own, compiled against the WHOLE of `app/Sources`
with `swift_build.py`'s line, cached by content, run
with a JSON request and answering with a JSON object. **A probe that will not
build is a scored FAILURE and never a `sys.exit`** — a rotted instrument must
not take the rest of the score down with it.

**The probe lives in an `.app` bundle, and exactly one of its six modes needs
that.** `NSApp.target(forAction:to:from:)` — the whole reason phase 8b's window
is an `NSPanel` — searches the KEY window's responder chain and then the MAIN
window's, and a process that cannot ACTIVATE has neither: measured, a bare
swiftc binary under `.prohibited`, `.accessory` or `.regular` reports
`keyWindow` nil and `mainWindow` nil after `makeKeyAndOrderFront`, and
`target(forAction:)` answers NONE for every mode, so the panel and the plain
window would look identical and the check would pass against both. Activation
needs a bundle and an `NSApplication.run()`, so `build_probe` wraps the binary
in one. **The `dispatch` mode therefore takes the keyboard focus for about a
second and puts two windows on screen while it runs.** Every other mode sets
`.prohibited` and orders nothing in, which is phase 7's posture.

What is claimed, section by section:

    1  **the aspect rule** (`PreviewQuality.renderSize(for:)`), which is the
       subtlest thing in the phase. Over eleven canvases, each at all three
       rows: the answer's aspect equals the canvas's EXACTLY, by integer
       cross-multiply and never a float tolerance; no answer is FINER than the
       row asked for; a coprime canvas (1001 x 667) comes back Full at every
       row; and the answer is always `m . (w/g, h/g)` for a whole `m`.
       **1920 x 1080 alone cannot fail any of this**, which is the whole
       reason 999 x 666, 1001 x 667, 100 x 100 and the portrait pair are in
       the list: a naive `(w/2, h/2)` is exactly right on 1920 x 1080 and
       wrong on three of the others. Then `PreviewQuality.stored()` with the
       key absent, at 0, 1 and 2, at 5 and -1 (outside the enum, which must
       read Full rather than trap) and at a STRING, plus the `store()` round
       trip.
    2  **the View menu**, in the same probe, because a menu lives in
       `NSApp.mainMenu` and is never drawn into a window (`phase6_chrome.py`'s
       reason). The menu ends with a separator, a `Preview Quality` submenu
       whose rows are `PreviewQuality.allCases`' titles carrying their raw
925:        title: "x", action: #selector(EditorViewController.exportProject(_:)), keyEquivalent: "")
927:        #selector(EditorViewController.exportProject(_:)), item: foreign) as Any
1057:        title: "x", action: #selector(EditorViewController.exportProject(_:)), keyEquivalent: "")
1059:        #selector(EditorViewController.exportProject(_:)), item: foreign) as Any
1144:        for name in ["exportProject:", "splitAtPlayhead:", "zoomToFit:"] {
1189:            where row.action == #selector(EditorViewController.exportProject(_:)) {
    finish()
    exit(0)
}
'''

INFO_PLIST = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" \
"http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
<key>CFBundleExecutable</key><string>phase8probe</string>
<key>CFBundleIdentifier</key><string>com.kgalligan.framejob.phase8probe</string>
<key>CFBundleName</key><string>Phase8Probe</string>
<key>CFBundlePackageType</key><string>APPL</string>
<key>NSPrincipalClass</key><string>NSApplication</string>
</dict></plist>
"""


def build_probe():
    """Compiles the probe through `swift_build.build` (reused when every input
    is byte-identical to a cached build's) into an `.app` bundle,
    which one mode needs and the rest merely tolerate (the script's header
    says why).

    Returns the binary's path, or None with the reason, which every section
    scores as a FAILURE rather than exiting."""
    focus by the window server about one time in three (measured, 30 retries
    over three seconds and never once), while every `open` of the same bundle
    activated. It is used by the `dispatch` mode alone, which is the only one
    that needs a key window at all."""
    if binary is None:
        return None, "the probe did not build"
    request_path = os.path.join(CHROME, f"request-{tag}.json")
    out = os.path.join(CHROME, f"answer-{tag}.json")
    if os.path.exists(out):
        os.remove(out)
    with open(request_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(request, f, indent=2)
    command = (["open", "-W", "-n", BUNDLE, "--args", request_path, out] if activate
               else [binary, request_path, out])
    start = time.time()
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        PROBE_RUNS.append((tag, False, timeout))
        return None, f"the probe did not return within {timeout} s"
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    if not os.path.exists(out):
        PROBE_RUNS.append((tag, False, elapsed))
        return None, (result.stdout + result.stderr).strip()[:600] or "no answer was written"
    with open(out) as f:
        answer = json.load(f)

The path doesn't follow the app. If you move Frame Job, copy the command again and register the new path.

The button isn't an edit, so no agent tool does the same thing.

### The missing helper warning

If the helper is missing from this copy of Frame Job, or can't be run, **Copy MCP Command** is dimmed and the status line reads "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."

Frame Job checks each time Settings opens. If the helper disappears while the window is open, pressing the button copies nothing and shows the same line.

## Testing a second copy

This is for testing, not everyday use. Setting the environment variable `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` to a path moves the socket there, so a test copy of Frame Job stays apart from your everyday one. Set it for both Frame Job and `framejob-mcp`.

Setting it for the helper alone is often enough. When a tool call finds nothing at that path, the helper launches the copy it belongs to and passes the path on. See [A custom socket path](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#a-custom-socket-path) for the rules.

To start a test copy yourself, run its executable from Terminal with the variable set:

```sh
RC_AGENT_SOCKET="$HOME/framejob-test/agent.sock" '/path/to/Frame Job.app/Contents/MacOS/Frame Job'
```

## Related

- [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/)
- [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/)

| `… not bound: <folder> is not a folder (a symlink is refused)` | The folder is a symlink. |
| `… not bound: could not make the folder <folder>: <reason>` | The folder is missing and can't be made, or a file is in its place. |
| `… not bound: <folder> is owned by uid 501, not this user (502)` | Someone else owns the folder. |
| `… not bound: <path> exists and is not a socket; it is left alone` | Something else is at the socket's path. Frame Job won't delete it. |
| `… not bound: socket path is 110 bytes; macOS allows 103: <path>` | A [custom path](#a-custom-socket-path) is too long. |
| `… not bound: socket path must be absolute: <path>` | A custom path doesn't start at the root. |

### A custom socket path

The environment variable `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` moves the socket, for both the app and the helper. It's for [testing a second copy](/mcp/connect-a-client/#testing-a-second-copy).

- The path must be absolute, and at most 103 bytes. That's a macOS limit.
- An empty value means the default path.
- The path's folder follows the same [rules](#the-sockets-folder-and-permissions) as the default one. A folder that already exists with mode `0755` won't do. A missing folder is made with the right mode.
- Only the socket moves. The test copy still shares your everyday copy's preferences.

When the helper launches Frame Job for a custom socket, it passes the path on, tells macOS not to restore the app's windows from last time, and writes the app's error output to `framejob-launch.log` beside the socket. A launch for your own socket does none of this, so your Frame Job opens as yours.

## When the helper launches Frame Job

The helper launches Frame Job when a [tool call finds nothing listening](/mcp/overview/#opening-on-the-first-tool-call). It runs `open -n -g` on its own app, so the app stays in the background. Nothing else launches it: not a client starting up, not `ping`, not a request for the tool list.

### One launch between several clients

Two clients that both find no Frame Job launch one copy between them, not two. A lock file, `agent.launch.lock`, sits beside the socket, and the helper holds it until the launched copy responds or the wait ends. Another helper waiting on that lock looks again once it gets it, and finds the copy already running.

Calls made at the same moment in one client session also launch at most once.

### The launch wait

The helper waits up to 60 seconds for a launched Frame Job to start listening. To change that, set the environment variable `RC_MCP_LAUNCH_WAIT` for the helper to a positive whole number of seconds. Any other value means 60.

def resources(here):
    """What W1–W3's real exports read beside the binary, as the app reads them
    from its bundle: `default.metallib`, compiled from the tree's shaders, and
    `Blank.mp4`, the placeholder track of a timeline with no media. None, or
    why one could not be made."""
    airs = []
    for shader in sorted(SHADERS.glob("*.metal")):
        air = here / (shader.stem + ".air")
        step = subprocess.run(
            ["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metal", "-c", str(shader), "-o", str(air)],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
        if step.returncode:
            return f"metal {shader.name}: {step.stderr[:300]}"
        airs.append(str(air))
    step = subprocess.run(
        ["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metallib", *airs, "-o", str(here / "default.metallib")],
        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
    if step.returncode:
        return f"metallib: {step.stderr[:300]}"
    shutil.copyfile(ROOT / "app/Resources/Blank.mp4", here / "Blank.mp4")
    return None


def build(sources, here):
    """(binary, None) or (None, why): `swift_build.build`, without the
    dev-tools flag (nothing here needs it), with `resources` beside it."""
    why = resources(here)
    if why:
        return None, why
    entry = here / "main.swift"
    shutil.copyfile(HERE / "tips_probe.swift", entry)
    binary = here / "tips-probe"
    swift = sorted(str(p) for p in sources.glob("*.swift") if p.name != "main.swift")
    if len(swift) < 100:
        return None, "app source set incomplete"
    try:
        swift_build.build(sources=swift + [entry], output=binary)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        return None, "swiftc: " + "; ".join(error.diagnostics[:8])
    return binary, None

    for tag, toggle, body, rows in (("on", "YES", on, ["L1", "L2"]), ("off", "NO", off, ["L3"])):
        if not set(rows) & set(wanted) and "L0" not in wanted:
            continue
        try:
            instance(binary, tag, toggle, session, results, body)
        except Exception as error:  # a row that could not run is that row's failure
            for row in rows:
                answers.setdefault(row, (False, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"))
    parity = results.get("parity", [])
    answers["L0"] = (
        len(parity) > 0 and all(not lines for _, lines in parity),
        "; ".join(f"{tag}: {lines[:2] or 'nothing'}" for tag, lines in parity) or "no instance ran")
    fail_all("not run")
    return answers


# ---- the run ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--sources", type=Path, default=ROOT / "app/Sources")
    parser.add_argument("--mutant", choices=sorted(MUTANTS))
    parser.add_argument("--only", help="comma-separated row ids")
    parser.add_argument("--no-live", action="store_true", help="leave the L rows out")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    named = MUTANTS[args.mutant][0] if args.mutant else []
    if args.only:
        wanted = args.only.split(",")
    elif args.mutant:
        wanted = ["B0"] + named
    else:
        wanted = [row for row in ROWS if not (args.no_live and row in LIVE_ROWS)]
    unknown = [row for row in wanted if row not in ROWS]
    if unknown:
        print("unknown row " + ", ".join(unknown))
        return 2
    if args.mutant and set(wanted) & set(LIVE_ROWS):
        print("a mutant is a probe rebuild; the L rows do not run under one")
        return 2
    here = WORK / (f"mutant-{args.mutant}" if args.mutant else "tree")
    if here.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(here)
    here.mkdir(parents=True)
    sources = args.sources.resolve()
    if args.mutant:
        why = mutate(sources, args.mutant, here / "Sources")
        if why:
            print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — {why}")
            return 2
        sources = here / "Sources"

    results = {}
    not_scored = []
    probe_wanted = [row for row in wanted if row in PROBE_ROWS]
    if "B0" in wanted or probe_wanted:
        binary, why = build(sources, here)
        results["B0"] = (binary is not None, why or f"built from {sources}")
        if binary is None and args.mutant:
            print(f"B0 fail — {why}")
            print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — the copy did "
                  "not build")
            return 2
        if probe_wanted:
            if binary is None:
                for row in probe_wanted:
                    results[row] = (False, "not run: the probe did not build")
            else:
                answer, why = probe(binary, here)
                rows = (answer or {}).get("rows") or []
                for row in probe_wanted:
                    found = next((a for a in rows if a.get("id") == row), None)
                    if found is None:
                        not_scored.append(row)
                        results[row] = (False, f"no row: {why or 'the probe did not answer it'}")
                    else:
                        results[row] = (bool(found["pass"]), found["detail"])
    if "T1" in wanted:
        results["T1"] = tree_row(sources)
    if set(wanted) & set(LIVE_ROWS):
        results.update(live(wanted))

    for row in wanted:
        good, detail = results[row]
        print(f"{row} {'pass' if good else 'fail'} — {detail}")
    passed = sum(1 for row in wanted if results[row][0])
    print(f"scores: {passed}/{len(wanted)}")
    if not args.mutant:
        return 0 if passed == len(wanted) else 1
    lost = [row for row in named if row in not_scored or row not in results]
    if lost:
        print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — "
              f"{', '.join(lost)} not scored")
        return 2
    survived = [row for row in named if results[row][0]]
    if survived:
        print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: SURVIVED — {', '.join(survived)} passed")
        return 0
    print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: CAUGHT — {', '.join(named)} failed")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

**The defaults guard** (issue batch B83, #238). No environment moves
`UserDefaults`, so every instance a proof drives shares its bundle's
defaults domain with the owner. The guarded domain is the bundle under
test's: `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for Release, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for Debug (`make app-debug`, spec §11 V-5). A record per socket path holds
that domain's key names against salted digests (`proof_defaults.snapshot`,
`defaults export` only) and the other Frame Job pids sharing it:
`scratch_socket()` records `proof_app.domain()`, the app `RC_PROOF_APP`
chooses, `launch()` re-records the binary's own and owns its child, and
`MCP()` records a socket it was handed. A socket `scratch_socket()` made and
`MCP()` then finds held by an instance of ANOTHER bundle (a script that
started the app itself on it) is re-homed to that bundle's domain, said on
stderr (`_rehome`); a write before that connect is not seen. The record and
the compare both read the domain with no `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` in `defaults`'
environment (`proof_defaults.read_env`): under one naming a folder that does not exist
`defaults export` answers no key, so a script run under a scratch home not
made yet at the record, or removed before the compare, would otherwise be
told every key of the domain moved (issue batch B84; `defaults_proof.py`
H1, H2). `remove_scratch()` compares, and one
`atexit` handler compares every record still held. A moved key outside
AppKit's `NS*`/`Apple*` families prints `mcp: DEFAULTS MOVED in <domain>:
<names> (other Frame Job pids: <list|none>)` on stderr; when no other Frame Job
shares the domain the script ENDS with status `DEFAULTS_EXIT` and those
lines last, and when one does it only prints. A value is never printed.
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. A handed socket whose file is there and
whose pid `lsof` cannot name is said on stderr, and a moved key is then only
printed unless `lsof` names the pid at the compare. A handed pid whose
bundle identifier cannot be read is said on stderr too: it is owned, and its
record guards the app's domain. A guard body that raised says so on stderr. A domain that cannot be
read is said on stderr. Not reached: a script killed by a signal or leaving
by `os._exit`."""

content.content:
## When Frame Job asks

Frame Job opens the Tips window by itself rarely, and only just after an export you made has finished.

- **The first time** comes once you've finished at least 5 exports and 30 days have passed since the first of them. If you press **Leave a Tip** before then, that counts as having been asked, and the next time is a December.
- **After that**, once a year, in December. If Frame Job asked, or you pressed **Leave a Tip**, after the start of June, it skips that year's December.

It appears when you close the result of an **Export…**, or when an export you added to the queue finishes. It never takes the keyboard, so a key you were typing can't press one of its buttons. Close it and it won't come back until the next time it's due.

Only exports you start from the export sheet count: **Export…** and **Add to Queue**. An export that fails or that you cancel doesn't count. Exports an agent or the Assistant starts don't count either, and they never open the window.

Opening the window yourself and choosing **Not Now** changes nothing about when Frame Job next asks.

## Turn tips off

Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** and find **Tips**, the last section.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder** | Shows the green **Tips** button in the toolbar and lets Frame Job open the Tips window by itself. Untick it to stop both. | On |
| **Tips** | Opens the Tips window. It's always there, whatever the box says. | |

The box saves the moment you click it, and the button leaves or returns in every open editor window at once.

## Good to know

- Frame Job keeps the count of your exports, the date of the first one and the date it last asked in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, on your Mac only.
- December is judged by your Mac's time zone.
- If you export nothing in December, Frame Job doesn't ask that year.
- No agent tool opens the Tips window or changes this setting.

## Related

- [Settings](/reference/settings/#tips)
----

**Clip ▸ Match Audio…** remembers none of its choices.

## Where these are kept

All of these live in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` domain. So do the model, the region, the compaction and clearing settings, **Background render** and the **Tips** box from the Settings window, and what [Tips](/reference/tips/#when-frame-job-asks) counts: how many exports you've finished, the date of the first, and the date Frame Job last asked. Your API keys are never stored there.

## Related

- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)

content.content:
**CH-5 — Settings' info buttons**
- **Do:** 1. Frame Job ▸ Settings…; hover each ⓘ beside "Assistant" and "Transcription", then move off. 2. Flick the pointer across an ⓘ without stopping. 3. Click one, then click elsewhere. 4. Click one, then click the same ⓘ again. 5. Rest on one until it opens, then click it and move off. 6. With Keyboard navigation on (System Settings ▸ Keyboard), Tab to an ⓘ and press Space. 7. With VoiceOver on, move to each ⓘ. 8. Close Settings with a popover up. 9. Repeat in both appearances, with Reduce motion on and off.
- **Expect:** a popover opens after a short beat, not on a flick across, and closes on leaving the icon; a second click on the ⓘ closes it (no flicker back open); a click on a hover-opened one keeps it open after the pointer leaves; the text is large and high-contrast, in short paragraphs, and wraps without clipping; VoiceOver says "About Assistant" / "About Transcription" and reads the text; the popover goes with the window.
- **Source:** issue batch B71 (spec §11 SH-5).

**CH-6 — Settings' MCP section**
- **Do:** 1. On a 13" display, open Frame Job ▸ Settings… in the light appearance and read the MCP section's blurb. 2. Press Copy MCP Command. 3. Scroll down to the Playback section's Background render row, if Settings scrolls. 4. Repeat in the dark appearance.
- **Expect:** the window fits on screen, top and bottom (on a display shorter than its five panes, such as 1440 × 900, the panes scroll and the Background render row is reached by scrolling); the blurb is large and high-contrast; the button is below the blurb; nothing is selected or highlighted when Settings opens (the Assistant key field has focus); the status line appears after a press.
- **Answer:** did the window fit, read clearly, open with nothing selected, and show the status line after the press, in both appearances?
- **Source:** issue batch B74 (#222; `settings_layout_probe.py` L9, L10; spec §11 MC-7); the scrolling, #127 G6 phase 4's fix pass 1 (`settings_layout_probe.py` L13; spec §11 G-38 (a)).

**CH-7 — The Tips button and its dialog**
- **Do:** 1. Open a project and look at the right end of the toolbar, in the light appearance. 2. Hover the green Tips button, then press it. 3. Read the window; press Not Now. 4. Press Tips again, then press Leave a Tip. 5. Select a clip that has an action, so the mint action lane and bands are on screen beside the button. 6. Narrow the window to its minimum width. 7. Repeat in the dark appearance.
- **Expect:** a green square "Tips" button after Export…, white label easy to read, lightening on hover, with the tooltip "Support Frame Job"; it reads as a different green from the action lane's mint in both appearances, and as a sibling of Export… in size. The Tips window is centred, titled Tips, reads as one of Frame Job's sheets (bold heading, a paragraph, a grey line naming Settings ▸ Tips, Not Now outlined and Leave a Tip blue), and nothing is clipped. Not Now closes it. Leave a Tip opens `https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/` in the browser and closes the window. At the minimum width nothing in the toolbar is squeezed or overlaps.
- **Answer:** is this green right beside the action ink, in both appearances, or should the button take another colour?
- **Source:** Tips (spec §11 TIP-1, TIP-2, TIP-6; `tips_proof.py` C1, C2).

**CH-8 — Settings ▸ Tips**

## Issue batch B83 — proofs and the owner's `UserDefaults` (`proof_defaults.py` P1–P9, P5s and three mutants; `defaults_proof.py` C0, G1–G5, R1, R2 and two mutants; `mcp.py`'s guard; #238)

B82 put four proofs' Application Support under a scratch home and measured
that this does not move `UserDefaults`. This batch closes #238 as measured:
no environment moves `UserDefaults`, a proof session moves no setting the
owner sees, and a probe's domain can only be removed after it exits. So
there are two things: a guard in `mcp.py` that FAILS a script whose session
moved a key, and a removal recipe with a gated sweep for the proofs' own
domains. No file under `app/`, `core/`, `graphic/`, `mcp-proxy/` or `agent/`
changed, and no spec §11 decision was made.

**Measured** (the designer, 2026-10-04, `70ccb86`, macOS 26.5.1; drivers not
kept; key names only):

- **(a) refuted.** A throwaway executable writing `UserDefaults.standard`, a fresh name per run,
  under `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`; that + `__CFPREFERENCES_AVOID_DAEMON=1` (scratch `Library/Preferences`
  absent, then pre-made); the variable alone; `HOME` + it; all three: every run left
  `~/Library/Preferences/<name>.plist` and nothing in the scratch home. `__CFBundleIdentifier` did
  not rename the domain; a `sandbox-exec` profile denying `com.apple.cfprefsd.*` did not stop it.
- **(b) in-process refuted; after exit it works.** `removePersistentDomain` in the process, or
  `defaults delete <name>` alone, leaves a 42-byte plist. `defaults delete <name>` (rc 0 or 1) THEN
  unlinking the plist, after the process exited, left no file and no domain at once and 10 s
  later, in five cases (with and without `synchronize`, with and without an in-process removal).
  Unlinking without the `defaults delete` after an in-process removal: the file came back.
- **(c) holds for the app's domain.** The real `com.kgalligan.Reelcut` (47 keys, by name and
  salted digest; another session's pid 85319 running; an 8 s no-launch control unmoved) was
  unmoved across a bare `mcp.launch`, `new_project` + `close_project`, and every clone session.

# second surprise: a bare swiftc probe never needs it, the signed app
    # does), and the camera's, added on that finding (spec §11 CAM-3: CR0
    # measured only a bare binary under the terminal's grant). The file is
    # GENERATED by xcodegen from these properties, like app/Info.plist, and
    # git-ignored beside it.
    entitlements:
      path: app/FrameJob.entitlements
      properties:
        com.apple.security.device.audio-input: true
        com.apple.security.device.camera: true
    preBuildScripts:
      # The bundled encoders (road map "codec-export" C0, spec §11 CX-5):
      # tools/codecs/build_codecs.py fetches, checks and builds SVT-AV1 and
      # libvpx into build/codecs/, or reuses them by its stamp (a no-op costs
      # well under a second), so the step runs every build. The PATH is Build
      # Rust Core's without cargo; the script also finds cmake in
      # /opt/homebrew/bin or /usr/local/bin when Xcode's PATH lacks Homebrew,
      # and builds under its own scrubbed environment, so this step and a
      # shell's `make codecs` compute one key.
      - name: Build Codecs
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: |
          set -e
          export PATH="/usr/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"

# Objections: exports over MCP count toward Tips

Checked against `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-tips2` at 6b373f3e. Two objections. The
plan's line citations under "What is true now" all hold.

## The two checks the orchestrator asked for

**(a) No ordinary path sets `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` on the app process: holds.**

- `framejob-mcp` adds `--env RC_AGENT_SOCKET=…` only when its own environment has the variable
  set and not empty (`mcp-proxy/src/launch.rs:49-67`, `:116`; `socket.rs:40-42`).
- Copy MCP Command writes no environment: `claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '<helper>'`
  (`app/Sources/AgentServer+Socket.swift:105-108`).
- The site names the variable in two places, both as testing a second copy
  (`docs/site/src/content/docs/mcp/connect-a-client.mdx:90-100`,
  `mcp/helper-and-socket.mdx:102-111`). `README.md` does not name it.
- Nothing in `app/Sources`, the `Makefile` (`run` is a bare `open`, `:221-222`) or `project.yml`
  sets it. The app only reads it (`AgentServer+Socket.swift:58`).

The same question for the plan's second variable, `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`, does not hold cleanly.
That is objection 1.

**(b) Every proof path that launches a real bundle sets `RC_AGENT_SOCKET`: holds.**

- `mcp.launch` sets it unconditionally (`tools/proof/mcp.py:609-610`). Every `Instance` wrapper
  goes through it, including the Release-only proofs: `precision_proof.py:2690`, `:3121`,
  `grading_verdict.py:662`, `co1_proof.py:682`, `reader_wedge_proof.py:483`,
  `constant_render_proof.py:445`, `recording_proof.py:784`, `av1_export_proof.py:527`.
- Every own-`Popen` of the app binary sets it: `agent_socket_proof.py:310`,
  `assistant_session_proof.py:254-255` (also when the folder is `0755` and nothing binds),
  `cloud_captions_proof.py:281`, `codec_import_proof.py:280`, `container_import_proof.py:461`,
  `defaults_proof.py:203`, `:403`, `export_cancel_proof.py:184`, `extreme_time_proof.py:228`,
  `frame_grid_proof.py:163`, `graphics_proof.py:407`, `graphics_prefetch_proof.py:187`,
  `graphics_store_proof.py:83`, `graphics_spike/rows_app.py:49`, `playback_prefetch_proof.py:200`,
  `screens.py:491`, `word_captions_proof.py:104`, `words_spike/scratch_rows.py:248`,
  `ai_docs_b2_proof.py:700`, `recording_spike.py:1710`.
- The launches through `open` pass it with `--env`: `mc1_spike.py:676`, `recording_spike.py:1725`,
  and `mcp_proxy_proof.py:215` through the helper.
- The app binary is run with neither variable in two places, and neither can export:
  `codecs_proof.py:57` (`-RCCodecProbe 1` prints and exits) and the Write Agent Catalog build
  step.
- The bundled probes (`phase8_chrome.py:1745`, the capture, cursor and camera spikes) have a
  bundle id and neither variable, but none calls `beginExport`, `enqueueExport` or the `export`
  handler.

## 1. `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` can reach a person's app, and no proof needs it

**Claim.** The plan says none of the three conditions is "something an MCP client sets by
accident" because "the helper passes the variable to the app only for a scratch socket". That
covers `--env` only. A person whose client runs under the App Sandbox would get an app that is
never counted and never asked, silently.

**Evidence.**

- `open(1)` says "Opened applications inherit environment variables just as if you had launched
  the application directly through its full path" (`man open`, line 26). The helper runs
  `/usr/bin/open` with its own environment untouched (`mcp-proxy/src/launch.rs:117-120`), so the
  app gets the client's whole environment.
- macOS sets `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` in sandboxed processes. On this Mac, 5 running processes carry
  it, all pointing under `Library/Containers` (`ps eww -ax`, counted, values not printed).
- No proof needs the condition. Every launch of a real bundle that sets `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`
  also sets `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` (see (b)). The launches with the home alone are bare probes
  (`tips_proof.py:268`, `precision_proof.py:1870`, `:2556`, `ai_docs_b2_proof.py:568`, `:625`),
  which the bundle condition already covers.
- Not verified: that `open` forwards the environment on this macOS (I ran nothing), and that a
  sandboxed client can run the helper at all. The repo has no measurement of either.

**Suggested change.** Drop the home condition from TIP-8, with `home-ignored` and I2, leaving
bundle and socket; or keep it and add the sandboxed-client case to TIP-8's accepted risks and
the site bullet.

## 2. The line that joins the rule to the doors is never seen failing

**Claim.** No probe row and no mutant covers `TipsDoors.init`'s default
`counts: { TipsInstance.isPersons }`, or `isPersons` reading the process's own environment. L2
is the only check, and it reports after the bundle's domain has already been written.

**Evidence.**

- W4, W5 and W6 inject `counts` (plan section 5). I1 to I3 call the pure `counts(environment:bundleIdentifier:)`.
- I3's second fact, the probe's own `isPersons` is false, holds for two independent reasons: the
  probe has no bundle id, and `tips_proof.py:268` sets `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`. So it cannot show
  that the environment is read.
- Mutants never run an L row (`tips_proof.py:475-477`).
- Scenario: the default is written `{ true }`, or `isPersons` passes `[:]` as the environment.
  Every probe row passes and all eighteen mutants are caught as designed. The first sign is L2
  on a live instance, after an agent export has written `FrameJobTipsExports` to the bundle's
  domain. That is the Debug domain if the plan's order of work is kept.
- The request asks for a mutant for "proof instance not counted".

**Suggested change.** Add a probe row that runs the queue door through a `TipsDoors` built with
the default `counts` (the probe is a scratch instance) and expects nothing counted or ordered,
with a mutant that replaces the default with `{ true }`.

verdict: revise

  bundle id and neither variable, but none calls `beginExport`, `enqueueExport` or the `export`
  handler.

accident" because "the helper passes the variable to the app only for a scratch socket". That
covers `--env` only. A person whose client runs under the App Sandbox would get an app that is
never counted and never asked, silently.

  the application directly through its full path" (`man open`, line 26). The helper runs

bundle and socket; or keep it and add the sandboxed-client case to TIP-8's accepted risks and

## 2. The line that joins the rule to the doors is never seen failing

**Claim.** No probe row and no mutant covers `TipsDoors.init`'s default
`counts: { TipsInstance.isPersons }`, or `isPersons` reading the process's own environment. L2
is the only check, and it reports after the bundle's domain has already been written.

  probe has no bundle id, and `tips_proof.py:268` sets `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`. So it cannot show
  that the environment is read.
- Mutants never run an L row (`tips_proof.py:475-477`).
- Scenario: the default is written `{ true }`, or `isPersons` passes `[:]` as the environment.
  Every probe row passes and all eighteen mutants are caught as designed. The first sign is L2
  on a live instance, after an agent export has written `FrameJobTipsExports` to the bundle's
  domain. That is the Debug domain if the plan's order of work is kept.
- The request asks for a mutant for "proof instance not counted".

**Suggested change.** Add a probe row that runs the queue door through a `TipsDoors` built with
the default `counts` (the probe is a scratch instance) and expects nothing counted or ordered,
with a mutant that replaces the default with `{ true }`.
